note: D6 `pull_line`, the new op (vine_whip+rake): the pull body run against every enemy on a dir line, nearest first, for one charge. The rake east from (1,2) collects the drill bot at (3,2) (id 1) then the one at (4,2) (id 2) in walk order - a deterministic order, no rng - and runs the ordinary pull against each: id 1 is hauled one tile to (2,2), which staggers it (a forced move blanks a telegraphed wind-up, which is the whip's real currency) and takes 2; id 2 is then hauled one tile to (3,2) and stops there because (2,2) is no longer _open - the enemy dragged adjacent BLOCKS the one behind it, each pull reading the live board. Two mutations fail this record in plain mode: breaking out of the loop after the first enemy drops patterns 4 and 5, and reversing the walk order (farthest first) makes id 2 collide before id 1 has moved, so the staggered/damage pairs come back in the other order. Unlike `pull`, an enemy that dies mid-line does not end the effect. The rake aims by `dir_enemy` (bump 13, still SIM_VERSION 13): the east cast is legal here only BECAUSE that line holds an enemy - a direction whose line holds none within range is not offered at all and the same action would come back {t: illegal}. Its four-direction legality is pinned by d6_rake_targeting.
